transcript.text: A persistent beep in a fridge-freezer is most often an alarm triggered because the appliance thinks the door hasn't shut properly, or because the temperature inside has risen above the safe limit. Before assuming a part failure, we need to rule out simple causes. Please check the freezer door seal (gasket). Run your fingers around it and look for any splits, gaps, or sections that have come away from the door frame. It might also be dirty, folded over, or blocked by food packaging preventing a tight close. Is the seal torn or detached, was it just dirty/folded (and is that now sorted), or does it look completely fine?
seal looks fine to me. the bottom drawer wasn't pushed in properly last night though, a bag was sticking out

That bag sticking out of the bottom drawer is very likely the cause. Most fridge-freezers have a sensor that detects if any door or drawer isn't fully shut, and they will beep continuously as a warning. It’s also possible the alarm was triggered because warm air got in while the drawer was open, raising the temperature. Please push the bottom drawer all the way back in to make sure it's latched correctly. Then look for a button on the control panel labelled 'Alarm', 'Sound', or similar and press it to silence the beep.
ok pushed it in. there's a button with a bell on it, pressed it and the beep stopped. the freezer number is still flashing -9 though, going down slowly

The number going down slowly is exactly what you want to see: it means the compressor is running and the cold is returning. Since the beep has stopped, this is no longer an emergency alarm but a recovery phase. Please leave the freezer alone for about 4–6 hours (or overnight if possible). Do not open the door or put warm food inside during this time. Once the number stops flashing and settles at -18°C (or whatever your normal setting is), it will be back to normal. If it still hasn't reached a stable cold temperature after 24 hours, then we would need to look deeper, but for now, just let it recover.
